P1.text: Add `$track(fn)` to brumate/signals: `$track<F extends (...args: never[]) => unknown>(fn: F): F`, compile-time only (the compiler removes the call, as for `$handler`). It marks fn as a derivation wherever the value flows: the compiler adds edges from fn's tracked reads (through callees, `$untrack` cuts them) to the prop, spread, object member or context site that carries it, and re-sends a fresh bound function as #395 does. A write in fn outside `$untrack` is a compile error; a write inside `$untrack` is allowed, so the J4 case works.

evidence.source: J2 compile of Parent.brm on the branch; packages/brumate/src/runtime/signals.ts:214-230
evidence.detail: evidence/compile-branch.txt: the update a marked prop needs is the same u3 function, 82 B raw, plus one table entry; no runtime code

estimate.unit: B gzip runtime; about 82 B raw per marked prop

P2.text: `$track` is allowed in any expression of a .brm script or markup and in .brm.ts module functions, as `$handler` is (components.md:301). Nesting it with `$handler` either way is a compile error. Its real target is what inference cannot see: function members of object or array literals passed as props, such as `opts={{ label: $track(nameOf) }}` (J5), and objects that module functions build. In `$setContext` it is allowed and changes nothing, because main already follows the reads of a function in a context object.

evidence.source: node run.mjs <main dist> ProvCtx.brm, ProvCtx3.brm, ProvCtx4.brm
evidence.detail: evidence/context-function.txt: on 0.4.0 a context function that reads state re-sends the context (g has u2), even when it also writes; a write-only function gets no update

P3.text: An unmarked function prop is inferred by option B, the rule contexts already follow on main: live when it reads state, `$untrack` cuts reads, `onX` event-kind props stay fixed, no write scan. No error and no warning for unmarked props. A non-`on` handler prop that reads state, such as `validate=matches`, is re-sent, which runs no child code when the child calls it only in a handler (J6). I do not propose the fully explicit form (P7): React Compiler retired the useMemo/useCallback markers, and only 1 of 957 .brm files changes (J7).

evidence.source: evidence/prior-art.md; evidence/context-function.txt
evidence.detail: Solid and Svelte 5 track a function at its call site with no marker on the function; React moved from manual markers to compiler inference; brumate contexts already infer this way on 0.4.0

O6.text: A compile-time marker that has to follow a function into object members, spreads, contexts and objects returned by .brm.ts functions is the indirection that compile-time tracking handled worst before: Svelte 4's `$:` missed reads moved behind a function or object, which is why Svelte 5 moved to runes with runtime tracking. A `$track` that the flow analysis loses (an object built in one function and passed through another) stays stale with no error, the same failure as an unmarked prop.

evidence.source: svelte.dev/blog/runes (Introducing runes, 2023-09-20); J5; J8
evidence.detail: Svelte's runes post: `$:` dependencies are found at compile time, so refactoring the code into a function breaks reactivity. In brumate J8 shows the compiler already loses writes through a context function, and J5 shows it loses an object member today

P10.text: Drop the `$track` marker (P1, P2) and option B (P3, P4, P5). Replace P7's parent-side marker with a type that the child declares (P11).

evidence.source: ledger Q1, Q4, O1, O5

P10.why: Q1: object-member function props are rare. O1 and Q4: B loops on callbacks under names without `on`. O6: a marker that must follow a value through objects and modules is the flow that compile-time tracking misses. A child declaration needs no such flow.

P11.text: Path (b) in its strongest form: `brumate/signals` exports the type `Derived<F extends (...args: never[]) => unknown> = F`, and the child writes it in `$props<T>`, e.g. `validate?: Derived<(value: string) => string | null>`. The child compiler reads that type in the same way it already reads `Bindable` and `Promise`. A prop typed as a plain function type is fixed in the child: no memo, markup or effect depends on it, so a re-send runs nothing and no callback loops. A `Derived` prop is a source, also for effects. Callers pass a plain function, with no wrapper and no new compile-time function.

In a Vite build, the project analysis (vite.ts analyze -> analyzeProjectProps, which already parses every child to compute liveProps) also gives each parent the `Derived` props of its children, and the parent emits updates only for those. Callbacks then ship no update or table entry, which answers O3's +26 to +47 B per callback prop.
